summary: Maanasa Visweswaran works in Indology and computational fields. She studied at the University of Hamburg and served there as a Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin (attested 2026).

Mabel Haynes Bode (1864–1922) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed a PhD at the University of Bern and studied widely across Europe before lecturing on Pali at University College London and SOAS University of London.

Madan Mohan Malaviya (1861–1946) worked in Indology. He studied at Muir Central College, the University of Calcutta (B.A.), and the University of Allahabad (LL.B.), founded Banaras Hindu University in 1916, and served as its Vice Chancellor from 1919 to 1938.

Madeleine Biardeau (1922–2010) was an Indology, religious studies, and philosophy scholar who studied at ENS de Sèvres and under K. A. Sivaramakrishna Sastri. She served as Professor of Indian Religions at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1956–1989).
Madhav M. Deshpande (born 1946) specializes in Indology and linguistics. A former student of Ludo Rocher, he held a professorship at the University of Michigan (attested 1976, 1997, and 2006–2009).

Madhav Sadashiv Gore (1921–2010) studied under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye at the University of Mumbai and later at Columbia University School of Social Work. He held a post at Jawaharlal Nehru University from around 1997 to 2002.
Madhu Khanna is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. She held posts at Jamia Millia Islamia and the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (both attested 2012).

Madhusudan Amilal Dhaky (1927–2016) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Fergusson College and later served as Associate Director (1976–1996) and director emeritus of research (~1999–2005) at the American Institute of Indian Studies.

Madhusudan Gupta (1800–1856) worked in Indology and medicine. He studied at Sanskrit College and the Medical College and Hospital, Kolkata, later teaching Ayurveda at Sanskrit College (~1830–1835) and holding a post at Medical College and Hospital (~1835–1856).
Madhusudan Kaul Shastri was an Indologist. He served as Superintendent of the Research and Archaeological Department in Jammu and Kashmir (attested 1918–1934 and 1943–1945).
Madhusudan Singh Vats (1896–1972) was a scholar in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology who succeeded Rakhal Das Banerji (Rakhaldas Bandyopadhyay).

Maggie Bickford specializes in Sinology and art history/archaeology. She studied at Bennington College, Yale, and Princeton, and held posts as Professor of East Asian Studies at Brown University (around 1987 and 1993) and Member at the Institute for Advanced Study (~1997–1998).

Mahadev Govind Ranade (1842–1901) was active in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Elphinstone College, the University of Mumbai, and Government Law College, Mumbai, and founded the Maharashtra Girls Education Society in 1885.
Mahananda Timilsina is an Indologist who completed a PhD at Nepal Sanskrit University by 2015 and held an academic post there.

Mahasi Sayadaw (1904–1982) was a Buddhist studies and religious figure who studied under teachers including Mingun Jetawun Sayadaw U Narada. He served as abbot at Taung-waing-galay Taik Kyaung (1941) and resident teacher at Mahasi Sasana Yeiktha (1947).

Mahendranath Gupta (1854–1932) was a scholar in religious studies and Indology. After studying at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta, he served as a professor at Ripon College (Surendranath College) from around 1884 to 1900.

Mahesh A. Deokar works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He has served as Professor and Head at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 2011–2021) and as Regional Representative for the Pali Text Society (attested 2026).

Mahesh Chandra Nyayaratna Bhattacharyya (1836–1906) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied under Edward Byles Cowell and served as Principal of Sanskrit College and University (attested 1882, 1894, and 1914).

Mahinda Deegalle (born 1961) studied at the University of Ceylon, Harvard, and the University of Chicago under Diana L. Eck, Frank E. Reynolds, and Wendy Doniger. He held posts at IIBS, McGill, Bath Spa, and Colgate University.
Mahiro Ito (born 1968) is a Buddhist studies scholar who has held professorships at Bukkyo University and Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026), having succeeded Norihiko Tanaka in 2021.
